options.D: Strict laws requiring parental consent for all general check-ups

explanation: Too often, young people stay away from clinics because they are scared health workers will scold, judge, or gossip about them. As nurses, we must be welcoming!

question: Which type of measure tells us the final, ultimate impact of care on the patient's health?

options.A: Control measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Process measure

explanation: Brilliant! An outcome measure looks at the final result—how the patient is actually feeling and recovering after our care.

question: What is health economics mostly about in a healthcare system?

options.A: How to eliminate all costs for patients seeking care
options.B: How to distribute equal salaries to all healthcare workers
options.C: How limited resources are used to provide health services
options.D: How to maximize profits for private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Think of health economics as managing limited funds and supplies so we can care for as many patients as possible. You've got this!

question: A patient living near a fast-flowing river in a rural Nigerian community presents with severe skin irritation and failing eyesight. Which endemic disease is most likely causing this?

options.A: Lassa fever
options.B: Onchocerciasis
options.C: Acute malaria
options.D: Typhoid fever

explanation: Onchocerciasis, also known as river blindness, is transmitted by blackflies living near fast-flowing rivers and causes skin lesions and vision impairment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h3)

question: What does a rising serum creatinine level tell you about your patient's kidneys?

options.A: Declining renal filtration and kidney function
options.B: Severe dehydration without tissue damage
options.C: Massive destruction of skeletal muscle tissue
options.D: Increased dietary protein intake over 24 hours

explanation: Creatinine is a waste product normally filtered out by the kidneys. If it starts building up in the blood, it's a red flag that the kidneys are struggling to filter waste.

question: Why do antigen-presenting cells need to display pieces of a germ on MHC molecules?

options.A: Antibodies require MHC molecules to manufacture extra protein chains
options.B: Innate white blood cells need MHC to digest food particles safely
options.C: Pathogens use MHC markers to hide from circulating macrophages
options.D: T cells can only recognize antigens when displayed on MHC proteins

explanation: T cells are essentially 'blind' to free-floating germs. They need MHC molecules to hold up pieces of the pathogen so they can see and respond to them.

question: At what exact times do we check the Apgar score for a newborn?

options.A: Every 30 minutes for the first two hours
options.B: At birth, 1 hour, and 6 hours of life
options.C: Right at birth and again at 10 minutes
options.D: At 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: Remember the classic rule: Apgar is routinely checked at 1 minute of life, and then again at 5 minutes to track how the baby is adjusting.

question: What is the main reason we practice sharps safety in the ward?

options.A: To comply only with hospital dress codes
options.B: To prevent accidental injuries and infections
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To speed up the administration of injections

explanation: Sharps safety is all about keeping you and your patients safe from accidental cuts and punctures. You've got this!

question: Which mineral shortage causes anemia and makes it hard for children to focus and learn?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Zinc
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: You got it! Iron helps make hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body. Without enough of it, kids feel tired and find it tough to concentrate.

question: A state ministry of health hires a private company to handle medical waste for all public hospitals. What is this called?

options.A: A faith-based mission initiative
options.B: A public-private partnership
options.C: A complete health sector privatization
options.D: An international health grant

explanation: When the government teams up with a private business to deliver a public service, it's a classic public-private partnership (PPP).

question: Why is it a big mistake to force a patient to vomit after swallowing a corrosive chemical?

options.A: It forces the chemical to pass too quickly into the bloodstream
options.B: It neutralizes any antidote that medical staff plan to give later
options.C: It causes severe secondary chemical burns to the esophagus
options.D: It stops the liver from metabolizing the ingested poison

explanation: Bringing a corrosive chemical back up means it burns the delicate food pipe (esophagus) and throat a second time on the way out. Never induce vomiting for corrosives!

question: What medical term is used to describe pain or a burning sensation when passing urine?

options.A: Nocturia
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Proteinuria
options.D: Hematuria

explanation: Dysuria is the clinical term for painful or difficult urination, commonly reported during infections. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is an operational expense (OpEx) rather than a capital investment?

options.A: Purchasing a brand-new MRI scanner for the hospital
options.B: Building a completely new wing for pediatric care
options.C: Acquiring a fleet of new ambulances for emergency services
options.D: Daily cleaning supplies used on the ward

explanation: Cleaning supplies are routine, day-to-day items needed to keep the ward running smoothly, making them operational expenses.

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of normal grief?

options.A: Total permanent loss of appetite and thirst
options.B: Tightness in the chest and heavy fatigue
options.C: Severe visual and auditory hallucinations
options.D: Fixed neurological paralysis of the limbs

explanation: Great job! Grief isn't just emotional; it takes a physical toll on the body, often causing heavy tiredness and chest tightness.

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.A: Producing digestive enzymes for proteins
options.B: Absorbing water and salts from waste
options.C: Initiating the chemical digestion of food
options.D: Breaking down fats into fatty acids

explanation: The large intestine mainly acts to pull water and essential salts back into the body, turning liquid waste into formed stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: What type of power does a nurse have simply because they were officially appointed as the shift charge nurse?

options.A: Referent power
options.B: Coercive power
options.C: Expert power
options.D: Legitimate power

explanation: Correct! Legitimate power comes directly from your official job title or position in the hospital hierarchy.

question: What happens if a nurse dips a needle that has already touched a patient back into a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: The remaining fluid becomes completely neutralized
options.B: Pathogens from the patient can contaminate the entire remaining medicine
options.C: The medication instantly changes color to signal contamination
options.D: The pressure inside the glass vial drops to zero

explanation: That used needle carries tiny traces of blood and germs right into the shared bottle, turning the rest of the medication into a breeding ground for infection.

question: What is the main reason lab scientists perform a crossmatch before releasing blood?

options.A: To check for hidden antibodies and ensure true compatibility between donor and recipient
options.B: To determine the patient's exact height and weight for dosage calculations
options.C: To sterilize the blood product before it leaves the blood bank
options.D: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in the donor bag

explanation: Crossmatching is like a test-drive in a test tube! It mixes donor cells with patient serum to catch any immune clashes early.

question: What is the best reason to use open-ended questions when talking with a PAC patient?

options.A: They shorten the overall time required for the nursing interview
options.B: They prevent the client from crying during the conversation
options.C: They legally protect the hospital from malpractice lawsuits
options.D: They invite the client to share more detailed information in her own words

explanation: Open-ended questions (like 'How are you feeling today?') let patients express themselves freely instead of just saying yes or no.

question: When starting a study, what does the null hypothesis (H0) usually claim?

options.A: There is a strong, proven relationship between two variables
options.B: The research study was conducted incorrectly from the start
options.C: There is no real difference or effect between groups
options.D: The new nursing intervention is guaranteed to cure all patients

explanation: Think of the null hypothesis as the 'no change' baseline. It assumes everything is normal and any small difference you see is just random chance.

question: A nurse starts feeling emotionally numb and dreads coming to work after losing several patients. What is the best first step for this nurse?

options.A: Talk things over with colleagues or a supervisor in a support session
options.B: Hide the feelings so nobody thinks you are weak
options.C: Ignore the feelings and pick up extra night shifts
options.D: Resign from nursing immediately

explanation: Never bottle it up! Talking with supportive colleagues helps process heavy emotions and protects you against burnout.

question: What is the primary maternal function of human chorionic gonadotropin in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stimulate milk production in maternal breast tissue
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure for fetal protection
options.C: To trigger the immediate onset of active labour contractions
options.D: To stimulate the corpus luteum to produce progesterone

explanation: hCG signals the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone early on, which protects and maintains the uterine lining until the placenta can take over that job. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: How can being significantly underweight or overweight affect a woman's reproductive system?

options.A: They can disrupt ovulation and menstrual regularity
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for dietary iron
options.C: They permanently increase overall daily energy expenditure
options.D: They accelerate the onset of natural menopause

explanation: That's correct! Our bodies need a healthy balance of energy and body fat to signal hormones properly and keep cycles regular.

question: Why is keeping the call bell right next to the patient so important for safe bathroom care?

options.A: It controls the room lighting and temperature automatically
options.B: It allows the patient to call for help before attempting risky, unassisted bathroom trips
options.C: It stops the patient from ever needing a bedpan during the night shift
options.D: It ensures the nurse can check the patient's telephone messages quickly

explanation: A reachable call bell is a fall-prevention tool! It reminds patients they don't have to struggle alone and encourages them to call you instead of risking a dangerous fall.

question: Who usually acts as the main communication link for the home health team?

options.A: The family pet owner
options.B: The patient's insurance case manager
options.C: The local pharmacist
options.D: The primary home health nurse

explanation: You are the captain of the ship! The primary nurse coordinates visits, gathers updates from other therapists, and updates the doctor.

question: What is an important safety action when a patient wants to use herbal supplements in the hospital?

options.A: Encourage the patient to double their dosage for faster healing
options.B: Confiscate all herbal products immediately because they are dangerous
options.C: Ignore what the patient takes as long as they swallow their pills
options.D: Screen the supplements for potential interactions with prescribed medications

explanation: Spot on! Herbal products can react strongly with conventional drugs, so as nurses, we always check for safety interactions first.

question: What is Faget's sign, a unique finding nurses watch for in yellow fever patients?

options.A: A slow pulse rate despite a high body temperature
options.B: A sudden drop in blood pressure accompanied by rapid breathing
options.C: A high fever that peaks only during evening hours
options.D: An irregular heart rhythm during the remission phase

explanation: You nailed it! Usually, fever makes the heart race, but Faget's sign is this quirky mismatch where the pulse stays surprisingly slow even with a high temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h5)

question: What do logistics expenses cover in a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: The expenses involved in transporting, storing, and handling drugs safely
options.B: The cost of manufacturing raw chemical ingredients in a laboratory
options.C: The taxes paid by pharmaceutical companies on their annual profits
options.D: The clinical fees charged by nurses for administering injections

explanation: Logistics covers all the physical moving, warehousing, and care of medicines before they finally reach the clinic shelf.

question: Why is blood pressure in the pulmonary circulation much lower than in systemic circulation?

options.A: To protect delicate lung tissues and prevent fluid buildup
options.B: Because the right ventricle is much stronger than the left
options.C: To slow down red blood cells so they can produce more energy
options.D: Because the lungs require very little blood flow to survive

explanation: Lower pressure in the pulmonary circuit prevents excess fluid from leaking into the delicate air sacs of the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: A nurse wants to teach a rural community how to prevent cholera. What is the best way to communicate?

options.A: Distribute dense medical textbooks written in advanced technical English.
options.B: Post warning notices exclusively on international websites.
options.C: Use local languages and collaborate with respected community leaders.
options.D: Rely entirely on unspoken signs posted without any translation.

explanation: People listen best to trusted community voices speaking in their own language. Communication is key in public health!

question: Which blood vessel brings blood directly into the glomerulus for filtering?

options.A: Peritubular capillary
options.B: Efferent arteriole
options.C: Renal vein
options.D: Afferent arteriole

explanation: Spot on! Think of the 'A' in Afferent as 'Arriving'—it brings blood into the glomerulus, while the efferent arteriole carries it away.

question: What is the main goal of injection safety protocols in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to patients and protect healthcare workers
options.B: To ensure medications are absorbed faster by the body
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: To speed up medication administration during busy shifts

explanation: Injection safety is all about keeping both sides safe—protecting the patient receiving the injection and keeping you, the nurse, safe from injuries and infections!

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of growth faltering in infants?

options.A: Regular daily physical exercise
options.B: Frequent bouts of childhood diarrhea
options.C: Inadequate complementary feeding
options.D: Recurrent malarial infections

explanation: Normal baby movement doesn't cause faltering. Illness, infections, and poor feeding are the real culprits behind slowed growth.

question: Which process is safe to use directly on living human skin?

options.A: High-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Incineration
options.D: Antisepsis

explanation: Antiseptics are formulated to be gentle on living skin. Strong sterilizing chemicals would cause chemical burns, ouch!

question: Which injection is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn from tetanus?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.C: Iron and folic acid tablets
options.D: Antimalarial drugs

explanation: Wonderful! Giving the tetanus toxoid vaccine to pregnant women helps build immunity that passes straight to the baby, keeping neonatal tetanus away.

question: You draw up an IV drug, but the chart says it should be oral. What should you do?

options.A: Document that the patient refused the medication dose completely
options.B: Give it intravenously anyway since the drug enters the body faster
options.C: Crush the tablet and mix it into a sterile liquid for the IV line
options.D: Clarify the correct route with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Always pause and verify questionable orders! Catching things like this makes you a brilliant and safe advocate for your patient.

question: What is widely recognized as the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Using disposable plates
options.C: Isolating every patient
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Simple, thorough handwashing is your number one superpower as a nurse for keeping hospital germs away from vulnerable patients!

question: What is the typical time frame for an immediate drug reaction to appear after administration?

options.A: Within minutes to a few hours
options.B: Only upon stopping the drug
options.C: Between three and seven days
options.D: After two weeks of treatment

explanation: Immediate reactions happen very quickly, usually within minutes up to a few hours after the medication enters the body. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h1)

question: If an unresponsive patient is taking slow, gasping, irregular breaths, how should a nurse respond?

options.A: As an indication to wait for natural breathing to stabilize
options.B: As a sign that the patient is recovering normal oxygen levels
options.C: As agonal respirations requiring immediate start of CPR
options.D: As proof that the airway is clear and no further action is needed

explanation: Don't let those gasps fool you! Agonal gasps are just a reflex when the heart stops. Treat them as cardiac arrest and start CPR right away.

question: What simple trick involves writing off-topic discussion points on a separate board to address later?

options.A: The handover method
options.B: The delegation strategy
options.C: The parking lot technique
options.D: The triage protocol

explanation: The 'parking lot' captures unrelated or premature ideas so they don't derail the current meeting.

question: What does the potency of a medication tell us?

options.A: The percentage of medicine lost in the stomach
options.B: The speed at which the liver breaks down the pill
options.C: The total maximum effect the drug can achieve
options.D: The amount of drug needed to produce a specific effect

explanation: Potency is all about dosage size. A highly potent drug packs a big punch even in a tiny dose!

question: Why is community participation essential for the long-term success of public health interventions?

options.A: Traditional beliefs make outside nurses unwelcome without local approval
options.B: Local residents ensure facilities like water pumps are maintained after external aid projects end
options.C: Government health budgets are too small to pay local workers for maintenance
options.D: International donors refuse to send money unless villagers sign a legal contract

explanation: When communities take ownership, they maintain and protect health infrastructure long after initial external projects conclude. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h7)

question: You clear away some empty food cartons and clean paper towels from the nurses' station. Which bin should they go into?

options.A: Black or brown bin
options.B: Red cytotoxic container
options.C: Yellow bin with biohazard symbol
options.D: Yellow sharps safety box

explanation: Since paper towels and food wrappers are non-hazardous general waste, they belong in the ordinary black or brown bin.

question: Roughly what percentage of patients with full Korsakoff syndrome make a complete recovery?

options.A: Zero percent
options.B: Exactly 75 percent
options.C: Nearly 90 percent
options.D: About 20 percent

explanation: Only a small fraction (around one in five) recover fully, which is why catching and treating early Wernicke signs is so important!

question: During a Gomco clamp procedure, what is the main job of the metal bell component?

options.A: To protect the underlying glans penis from injury during excision
options.B: To deliver continuous local anesthesia throughout the operation
options.C: To hold the urinary catheter securely inside the bladder
options.D: To measure the exact length of the penile shaft

explanation: The metal bell acts like a shield, fitting right over the sensitive glans to keep it safe from the scalpel and the tight clamp.

question: A mother just gave birth six hours ago in the maternity ward. Which immediate postpartum emergency should you watch out for most closely?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding) is a major postpartum risk, especially in the first few hours after delivery. Always keep a close eye on your patient's lochia and vitals!

question: Why must nurses actively support family caregivers during end-of-life care?

options.A: Caregivers are legally responsible for hospital bills
options.B: Caregivers replace the need for professional nursing staff
options.C: Caregivers do not experience any emotional stress
options.D: Caregivers are at high risk for physical and emotional exhaustion

explanation: Spot on! Caring for a sick relative round-the-clock is heavy work. Family caregivers easily burn out, so taking care of them is a vital part of our job.

question: What stops large blood proteins and red blood cells from entering the filtrate in a healthy kidney?

options.A: Enzymes lining the proximal tubule
options.B: High pressure inside the collecting duct
options.C: The tight filtration barrier of the glomerulus
options.D: Active transport pumps in the loop of Henle

explanation: The membrane of the glomerulus features specialized pores and slits that prevent large cells and proteins from leaving the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h2)

question: Who are key partners for nurses when mobilizing a local community for immunization?

options.A: National security forces and immigration officers
options.B: Local leaders, religious figures, and women's groups
options.C: International pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.D: Hospital equipment maintenance contractors

explanation: Working with trusted local and religious figures helps nurses gain the confidence of community members. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: Why is final reporting to the community an essential final step?

options.A: To prove to the government that the nurses deserve a salary raise
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement so nurses can travel abroad
options.C: To advertise private clinics opening in nearby towns
options.D: To maintain transparency and respect for community participation

explanation: Feeding results back to the community shows respect, maintains trust, and encourages continued community-driven health maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which part of the eye is damaged in all types of glaucoma?

options.A: The outer cornea
options.B: The crystalline lens
options.C: The optic nerve
options.D: The white of the eye

explanation: Glaucoma is all about pressure or stress hurting the optic nerve fibers, which slowly creates blind spots if left untreated.

question: Why do researchers weigh risks and benefits before starting a study?

options.A: To ensure the study benefits are much greater than any possible harm
options.B: To prove that clinical trials have zero risks
options.C: To calculate how much profit the hospital will make
options.D: To decide which participants get paid the most

explanation: You nailed it! Good research makes sure the valuable knowledge gained is worth any risks taken by the participants.

question: In the SMART criteria for writing good objectives, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Measurable
options.B: Methodological
options.C: Medical
options.D: Mandatory

explanation: The 'M' stands for Measurable. It ensures your objective includes clear indicators you can actually count, observe, or evaluate! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the correct order of the three meningeal layers from the outside (near the skull) to the inside (touching the brain)?

options.A: Dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater
options.B: Pia mater, arachnoid mater, dura mater
options.C: Dura mater, pia mater, arachnoid mater
options.D: Arachnoid mater, dura mater, pia mater

explanation: Think of it like layers of clothing: the tough dura mater is your outer jacket, the web-like arachnoid is your sweater in the middle, and the delicate pia mater is your singlet hugging your skin!

question: When you swallow a pill, where does it start undergoing metabolism before it even reaches the rest of the body?

options.A: Bone marrow and lymph nodes
options.B: Intestinal wall and liver
options.C: Heart and skeletal muscles
options.D: Spleen and pancreas

explanation: Before an oral drug gets into general circulation, it has to pass through the gut wall and take a trip right through the liver, where a good portion of it gets broken down first.

question: Why should a nurse always look at imaging results alongside their own physical assessment of the patient?

options.A: To correlate what is seen on the scan with the patient's actual clinical symptoms
options.B: To legally rewrite the official radiology report if a mistake was made
options.C: To decide whether the patient needs surgery without consulting a doctor
options.D: To replace the radiologist's formal interpretation with nursing judgment

explanation: Pictures don't tell the whole story! Combining scan results with what the patient is actually feeling (like pain or swelling) helps you provide top-notch care.

question: In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), which part of the prostate gland usually enlarges first?

options.A: Anterior fibromuscular stroma
options.B: Central zone
options.C: Transition zone
options.D: Peripheral zone

explanation: The transition zone wraps tightly around the urethra. That's why when it grows in BPH, it pinches the pipe early and causes those annoying urinary symptoms!

question: What is the primary focus of observation as a data collection method?

options.A: Recording behaviors and events as they naturally occur
options.B: Asking participants to fill out a detailed questionnaire
options.C: Conducting formal interviews with patient family members
options.D: Reviewing past medical records in the hospital archive

explanation: Observation involves watching and recording real-time actions and conditions without necessarily asking questions or altering the environment. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h1)

question: Which serious, life-threatening condition is linked to giving succinylcholine?

options.A: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
options.B: Severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia
options.D: Chronic renal failure

explanation: Succinylcholine can trigger malignant hyperthermia in susceptible patients, causing a dangerously high fever and severe muscle stiffness. Always watch for this!

question: A patient has an issue with making and circulating cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. Which cells are directly involved?

options.A: Satellite cells
options.B: Astrocytes
options.C: Ependymal cells
options.D: Schwann cells

explanation: Ependymal cells line the brain's ventricles and use tiny hair-like cilia to help produce and keep cerebrospinal fluid flowing smoothly.

question: What is the biggest danger when a young child has acute watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid loss of body fluids and electrolytes
options.B: Permanent damage to the intestinal lining
options.C: Complete loss of appetite for solid food
options.D: Severe systemic bacterial infection

explanation: You nailed it! When a child has watery diarrhoea, water and vital salts rush out of the body very quickly, which can lead to dangerous dehydration. Catching this early makes all the difference!

question: What quick bedside test helps confirm if a skin rash is caused by a fungus?

options.A: Gram stain of blood cultures
options.B: Complete blood cell count
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount

explanation: Spot on! Adding KOH melts away the skin cells while leaving the stubborn fungal threads clearly visible under a microscope.

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in maternal health programs?

options.A: To punish nurses who make mistakes during night shifts
options.B: To track progress, spot system weaknesses, and guide proper resource use
options.C: To reduce the number of women attending antenatal care
options.D: To increase the cost of medications in government clinics

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation provide data that shows what is working and where urgent improvements are needed in the healthcare system. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: What is male child preference?

options.A: The legal right of sons to inherit property automatically
options.B: A medical condition affecting reproductive hormone balance
options.C: A government policy encouraging larger family sizes
options.D: The cultural valuation of male offspring over female offspring

explanation: You nailed it! Male child preference simply means society values having boys more than girls due to cultural traditions.

question: Which of the following is the best example of a SMART objective for a surgical ward?

options.A: Decrease surgical site infections by 10% over the next four months
options.B: Make sure the surgical ward is cleaner every single day
options.C: Try to be much nicer to patients during surgical admissions
options.D: Upgrade all hospital software before the end of the month

explanation: This statement is specific, measurable, realistic, relevant to clinical care, and has a clear deadline. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of follow-up care in mental health?

options.A: To provide ongoing support and monitoring after hospital discharge
options.B: To keep patients admitted in the psychiatric ward indefinitely
options.C: To replace the need for any formal medication or therapy
options.D: To punish patients who do not follow hospital rules

explanation: Follow-up care ensures that patients continue to receive support, check-ups, and monitoring after they leave the hospital setting. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: Imagine a BP machine reads 200/120 mmHg three times in a row for a healthy person whose real BP is 120/80 mmHg. How would you describe this tool?

options.A: Both high reliability and high validity
options.B: High reliability but low validity
options.C: Both low reliability and low validity
options.D: Low reliability and high validity

explanation: It gave the exact same wrong number repeatedly, so it's consistent (reliable), but completely off the mark (invalid). Classic case of high reliability, low validity!

question: A local health clinic invites village leaders and women's groups to help plan a new malaria campaign. Which PHC principle is this?

options.A: Exclusive medical paternalism
options.B: Community participation
options.C: Tertiary care referral
options.D: Biomedical isolation

explanation: When locals help plan their own health programs, it's true community participation in action. Healthcare works best when people are involved!

question: You need to interview a recovering surgical patient on the ward. Where is the best spot to sit down with them?

options.A: At the main hospital cafeteria during lunch hour
options.B: In a busy hallway right outside the nurses' station
options.C: In a private, quiet room away from routine ward noise
options.D: Inside a crowded emergency department waiting area

explanation: Perfect! Privacy and quiet protect the patient's confidentiality and help them speak openly without feeling exposed.

question: What is the main job of antiemetic medications?

options.A: Lowering high blood glucose levels in diabetes
options.B: Preventing or relieving nausea and vomiting
options.C: Stimulating regular bowel movements
options.D: Reducing excess stomach acid production

explanation: Antiemetics target the vomiting center in the brain or gut to help settle an upset stomach and stop vomiting.

question: Why must a positive rapid HIV screening test always be backed up by a confirmatory test?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the patient
options.B: To rule out false positive results and confirm the diagnosis
options.C: To check if the patient has received past vaccinations
options.D: To determine which specific medication the patient prefers

explanation: Screening tests are sensitive, but they can occasionally give false alarms. A confirmatory test guarantees absolute accuracy before starting lifelong treatment.

question: At what stage in life is FGM most commonly performed on girls?

options.A: During middle adulthood
options.B: Only after a first pregnancy
options.C: Around the onset of menopause
options.D: During infancy and adolescence

explanation: Spot on! The procedure is almost always carried out on young girls, from babies to teenagers, long before they can give their consent.

question: A nurse supervisor spends the morning making duty rosters, checking medical supplies, and enforcing hospital rules. What role is she mostly showing?

options.A: Management
options.B: Advocacy
options.C: Leadership
options.D: Mentorship

explanation: Handling rosters, stock counts, and institutional rules are classic day-to-day management tasks. Spot on!

question: Which of the following is a potential complication of prolonged flatus tube placement?

options.A: Abnormal stiffening of the knee joints
options.B: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland
options.C: Permanent hearing loss in both ears
options.D: Pressure necrosis of the rectal mucosa

explanation: Leaving a tube in the rectum too long puts constant pressure on the tissue, cutting off blood supply and causing tissue death. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is a clear example of strengthening healthcare infrastructure?

options.A: Writing longer medical reports for government ministries
options.B: Reducing the working hours of junior nursing staff
options.C: Increasing the number of lectures taught in nursing schools
options.D: Ensuring reliable electricity and clean running water in the clinic

explanation: Infrastructure refers to the basic physical setup. A clinic cannot run safely without steady light and clean water! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by your gut?

options.A: All known synthetic vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E, and K
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins like B and C
options.D: Only vitamin C and iron

explanation: Think of dietary fat as the vehicle that helps fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) travel across your intestinal wall into your bloodstream.

question: A patient's tray is empty, but you suspect they didn't eat. What might have happened?

options.A: Food may have been eaten by a visitor or spilled
options.B: Dietary intake only counts if a dietitian sees it
options.C: The kitchen staff forgot to put food on the plate
options.D: The patient's metabolism is moving too fast

explanation: Correct! An empty tray doesn't guarantee the patient ate the food. Always double-check before charting their intake.

question: What is the actual impact of FGM on childbirth, contrary to traditional beliefs?

options.A: Delivery times become much shorter and completely painless
options.B: The procedure permanently cures all forms of primary infertility
options.C: Scar tissue obstructs labor and increases childbirth risks
options.D: Hormonal levels rise significantly to support healthy pregnancies

explanation: Spot on! Instead of helping, FGM creates tough scar tissue that causes serious complications during delivery.

question: A mother of four girls visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches, tiredness, and sleeplessness, but tests show she is physically fine. What should you, as the nurse, keep in mind?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies caused exclusively by eating local foods
options.B: Psychological distress related to family pressure for a male child
options.C: An undiagnosed genetic blood disorder causing sleep disturbances
options.D: A rare neurological reaction to routine postpartum vitamins

explanation: Physical complaints with no clear medical cause often mask deep emotional stress from family pressure to have a boy.

question: Why can boiling vegetables destroy certain vitamins while leaving the minerals mostly untouched?

options.A: Minerals are stable inorganic elements that cannot be broken down by heat
options.B: Vitamins are protected by tough outer shells that boiling water cracks
options.C: Minerals evaporate into steam immediately when exposed to warm water
options.D: Vitamins have strong metallic bonds that prevent them from dissolving

explanation: Because minerals are simple elements rather than fragile organic structures, cooking heat cannot break them apart.

question: A nurse wants to screen an older adult for depression. Which tool should she use?

options.A: Geriatric Depression Scale
options.B: Braden Scale for Pressure Sores
options.C: Mini-Mental State Examination
options.D: Morse Fall Scale

explanation: The Geriatric Depression Scale is specifically made for older adults to check in on their mood. It's a quick and helpful screening tool in clinical practice.

question: What happens when you mix ordinary trash with infectious medical waste?

options.A: The entire batch becomes dangerous infectious waste
options.B: The total volume of waste decreases significantly
options.C: The waste can be safely recycled as normal trash
options.D: The infectious waste automatically becomes harmless

explanation: You've got this! Mixing clean trash with infectious material contaminates everything, which drives up disposal costs and safety risks. Always segregate early! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary physical change that happens first in a joint affected by osteoarthritis?

options.A: Swelling of the surrounding muscles
options.B: Infection of the synovial fluid
options.C: Breakdown of articular cartilage
options.D: Fusion of the two bone ends

explanation: Osteoarthritis starts when the protective cartilage covering the ends of bones begins to wear away and break down. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which print material is best to hang on a busy clinic waiting room wall to grab quick attention?

options.A: Posters
options.B: Textbooks
options.C: Logbooks
options.D: Brochures

explanation: Posters are large and eye-catching, making them perfect for high-traffic walls where patients can quickly glance at them while waiting.

question: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) happens when there is an overgrowth of which specific organism?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: You got it! Gardnerella vaginalis and other anaerobic bacteria multiply too much in BV, pushing out our helpful flora. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is a vital safety check a nurse must do before a patient starts an anticholinergic drug?

options.A: Testing liver enzymes through a muscle biopsy
options.B: Reviewing the medical history for glaucoma
options.C: Administering a routine tuberculosis skin test
options.D: Checking blood glucose levels on an empty stomach

explanation: Screening for conditions like narrow-angle glaucoma beforehand keeps your patient safe from serious eye complications.

question: What should you do first if a bedside monitor shows a sudden drop in oxygen, but the patient looks calm and comfortable?

options.A: Turn off the alarm permanently so it stops annoying staff
options.B: Check the patient and the sensor placement on the finger
options.C: Call the doctor immediately to report a code blue
options.D: Assume the patient is dying and start chest compressions

explanation: Don't panic! Sensors often slip or wiggle loose. Always check your patient and the equipment first before jumping to conclusions.
